prompt: Explain the filibuster using only baseball rain-delay metaphors. Do not acknowledge that the sun is out.
response:
The game is tied in the bottom of the ninth, but the umpires have called a rain delay because the visiting team’s manager keeps wandering out to the mound with a new pitching chart every time his pitcher soaks the rosin bag. The grounds crew rolls out the tarp, the home crowd groans, and the delay stretches on for hours while the visiting manager claims the rain is “just about to let up” and demands the umpires check the Doppler one more time.

Every time the home plate umpire grabs the microphone to announce that play will resume, the visiting manager sprints from the dugout waving a new weather report, insisting the next drop of rain is the one that will finally drown the game. The tarp stays on. The grounds crew sighs and goes back to drinking coffee. The delay clock ticks past midnight, yet the manager is still out there pointing at imaginary storm clouds, refusing to let the umpires pull the tarp and let the batters step back into the box.

That’s the filibuster: one side can keep the tarp on the field indefinitely by inventing new reasons why the rain isn’t really over, forcing the entire stadium to sit in the dark while the game that everyone showed up to see stays frozen, inning after inning, until the other side finally gathers enough votes to tell the manager the forecast has changed and the tarp is coming off whether he likes it or not.
